newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV REACHES PARIS OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV REACHES PARIS OPEN FINAL.

text.p: French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov stayed on course to become the first player to hold France's top two tennis titles when he reached the Paris Open final on Saturday.
The fourth-seeded Russian, who will climb to third in the world rankings published on Monday, beat Czech qualifier Petr Korda 3-6 6-4 6-2 in the first semifinal of the Bercy tournament.
He will meet one of two Swedes, Thomas Enqvist or Magnus Gustafsson, in Sunday's final.

Korda, French Open finalist in 1992, converted his first break point of the match to go 5-3 up in the first set. He then served for the set which he took on his second match point when Kafelnikov netted a return.
Kafelnikov, also holder of the Lyon title, struggled to get into the match and squandered an early break of service in the second set when he allowed Korda to break back immediately.

The match finally hinged on the failure of Korda, coming back from a long injury layoff, to convert three break points in the ninth game of the second set that would have set him up to serve for the match.
Kafelnikov went on to level the match with the first of three set points, his opponent driving the ball wide.
Korda also squandered two break points in the opening service game of the final set.
Kafelnikov never looked back after an early break in the deciding set but said afterwards that he he had to "play not 100 percent but 150 percent" to beat Korda.
"I felt he was tiring and wanted to win in two sets. Playing in the doubles takes a lot out of him. He finished very late last night.
"At first he was playing out of his mind, hitting winners all the time. I was just trying not to look a fool."
The semifinal was Korda's 11th match at Bercy since last Saturday, including singles qualifiers and doubles.
